notes.text: In Lev. 27:30-33, the Lord instructed Moses that the Israelites should give a "tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree" and a "tithe of the herd, or of the flock." Elsewhere, the tithe was considered to consist of "the corn [grain] of the threshing floor," the product "of the winepress" (Num. 18:26-28), and "the firstlings of your herds and of your flocks" (Deut. 12:5-6; 14:22). In 2 Chr. 31:4-6, we read that the Israelites gave tithes of "corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field... tithe of oxen and sheep, and the tithe of holy things which were consecrated unto the Lord their God." Neh. 10:37-39 speaks of "the firstfruits of our dough... the fruit of all manner of trees, of wine and of oil... and the tithes of our ground... the offering of the corn, of the new wine, and the oil." Corn, wine, and oil are also listed as tithes in Deut. 12:17 and 14:22-23 and in Neh. 13:5, 12. (Masada and Religion in First-Century Judea, BYU Studies, vol. 36 (1996-97), Number 3--1996-97)
